title: B05: Search file contents
prompt: **B05 — Search file contents.** Find selected words and patterns across synthetic sample files. Submit a short script or lab note with the goal, commands/steps, expected versus observed output, exit status or errors where relevant, and a tested boundary/failure case. Run only on synthetic inputs, an explicitly authorized lab, or a disposable VM. For state-changing work, take a snapshot/backup first and prepare recovery steps. CodeLeaf does not execute arbitrary Linux/Bash submissions inside its web process.

starter.execution_mode: manual-terminal; local Linux VM/WSL or separately isolated runner required
starter.starter:
# B05: Search file contents
# Define expected result and safe test scope before running commands.

public_tests.name: Topic token gate
public_tests.note: Lightweight grading gate checks for 'grep'; passing it does not establish runtime correctness.

acceptance_criteria: The exercise demonstrates the stated Section C outcome, not merely a copied command.
A repeatable verification is provided with expected and observed results.
At least one boundary/failure case is handled and explained.
State-changing steps stay within a disposable or explicitly authorized lab, with backup/rollback steps documented.
hints: Begin with read-only checks; use the target command manual and distribution documentation.
Use synthetic inputs and preview changes before applying them.
Capture exit status and errors; explain any step that was not executed.

retry_policy.guidance: Use review feedback to improve the explanation and rerun the safe local test; the text gate is not a runtime guarantee.

expected_output: Find selected words and patterns across synthetic sample files.
status_note: Directly mapped from Linux.pdf Section C; draft only and requires technical/human review before publication.
